evidence: Suet. Tit. 3: notīs quoque excipere vēlōcissimē solitum, to take down in shorthand (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Catching words as they are spoken, from a lecture or a speaker.
Built on commentārius, which in Quintilian (3.6.59) is a pupil’s notes of a lesson (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Col. 12.3.4 (Lewis & Short): ut meminisset atque adnotāret, quid et quandō et cui dedisset
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: only in post-Augustan prose.

terms.gloss: a note, a mark, a written sign

evidence: Plin. Ep. 1.6.1: meditābar aliquid ēnotābamque (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Post-Augustan and rare, says Lewis & Short: Pliny uses it of jotting down what he thought of while out hunting.

terms.gloss: make a note of, write down
evidence: Plin. Ep. 3.5.10: liber legēbātur, adnotābātur (Lewis & Short s.v. annotō)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short prefers the spelling adn-; only in post-Augustan prose.
